content.text: Activating a sidebar navigation item keeps the application within the same page instead of routing away.

expected_answer.operand: application routing, separate dashboard pages, navigation to another URL, or a multi-page workflow caused by sidebar navigation

content.text: The PRIMARY sidebar section contains Overview, Portfolio, Markets, Watchlist, and Transactions.

expected_answer.operand: the PRIMARY sidebar section shows Overview, Portfolio, Markets, Watchlist, and Transactions

content.text: The ANALYTICS sidebar section contains Performance, Risk, Attribution, and Scenarios.

expected_answer.operand: the ANALYTICS sidebar section shows Performance, Risk, Attribution, and Scenarios

content.text: The RESEARCH sidebar section contains Research Notes, Saved Views, and Reports.

expected_answer.operand: the RESEARCH sidebar section shows Research Notes, Saved Views, and Reports

content.text: The SYSTEM sidebar section contains Alerts and Data Health.

expected_answer.operand: the SYSTEM sidebar section shows Alerts and Data Health

content.text: Overview is the default selected sidebar item when the workspace first loads.
Activating a sidebar item changes the active sidebar state to the clicked item.

expected_answer.operand: the active sidebar item changes from the previously selected item to the clicked item

content.text: Activating a sidebar item changes the contextual page heading without leaving the current page.

expected_answer.operand: the contextual page heading changes from the previous heading while the application remains on the current page

judgements.rationale: [risk_factors] Applied user-reach because sidebar navigation is a core shell capability every investment professional uses, and change-frequency because navigation wiring and SPA behavior are common frontend change surfaces. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the cited source explicitly describes a static frontend benchmark with deterministic local mock data and no authentication or real trading.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because missing PRIMARY navigation items would block common dashboard movement. Did not apply change-frequency because the item inventory itself is less volatile than click behavior, and did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the source describes a static frontend benchmark without those concerns.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the ANALYTICS navigation set is part of the common shell exposed to all users of this use-case. Did not apply change-frequency because the section inventory is a fixed content contract in the cited sidebar specification, and money, auth, and data-loss do not apply in the benchmark source.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the RESEARCH navigation set is part of the shared dashboard shell. Did not apply change-frequency because the section inventory is stated as fixed sidebar content, and money, auth, and data-loss do not apply in the benchmark source.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because SYSTEM entries are part of the same shared sidebar contract. Did not apply change-frequency because the inventory is a fixed sidebar list in the current source, and money, auth, and data-loss do not apply in the benchmark source.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the default selected context shapes the first impression of the dashboard shell, and change-frequency because default-state regressions are common when navigation state is refactored. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the source is a static frontend benchmark.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because active-state feedback is essential to everyday navigation, and change-frequency because active-state management is a frequent frontend change surface. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the source defines a static frontend benchmark without those business risks.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the contextual page heading is the user's confirmation that the workspace changed context, and change-frequency because heading binding often changes with navigation wiring and content refactors. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the source defines a static frontend benchmark without those risks.
